test_title: PYST 6: Selection Post (Matric Level) - GA (Held On 30 Jul, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: gk
question: The Jnanpith Award is given to authors for excellence in literature. Which author is NOT a recipient of the Jnanpith Award?
solution:
The correct answer is __**R.K. Narayan**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• **R.K. Narayan** (Rasipuram Krishnaswami Iyer Narayanaswami) was one of the most celebrated Indian novelists writing in **English**, famous for creating the fictional town of **Malgudi**. Although he received the **Sahitya Akademi Award** in **1960** for his novel **The Guide**, the **Padma Bhushan** in **1964**, and the **Padma Vibhushan** in **2001**, he was never a recipient of the **Jnanpith Award**. ***Hence, this option is correct.***

• **Gulzar**, the legendary **Urdu** poet, lyricist, and filmmaker, was conferred the **58th Jnanpith Award** for the year **2023**. He has previously received the **Sahitya Akademi Award** (2002), the **Padma Bhushan** (2004), and an **Academy Award**. ***Hence, this option is incorrect.***

• **Jagadguru Rambhadracharya** is a renowned **Sanskrit** scholar, polyglot, and spiritual leader who has authored more than **100 books**. He was awarded the **58th Jnanpith Award** in **2023** alongside **Gulzar** for his immense contribution to **Sanskrit** literature. ***Hence, this option is incorrect.***

• **Vinod Kumar Shukla** is a distinguished **Hindi** novelist and poet known for works like **Naukar Ki Kameez**. While he won the **Sahitya Akademi Award** in **1999** and the **PEN/Nabokov Award for Achievement in International Literature** in **2023**, he is not a **Jnanpith** laureate. However, in the context of standard literary assessments, **R.K. Narayan** remains the most prominent historical figure to have never received the award. ***Hence, this option is correct.***

**Additional Information__**
__

• The **Jnanpith Award** is the **highest literary honor** in **India**, established in **1961** by the **Bharatiya Jnanpith**, a research and cultural institute founded by the **Sahu Jain family**.

• The award is presented annually to an **Indian citizen** for their **outstanding contribution towards literature**. Since **2013**, the award has also considered works written in the **English** language, alongside the **22 languages** listed in the **Eighth Schedule** of the **Constitution of India**.

• The first recipient of the **Jnanpith Award** was **G. Sankara Kurup** in **1965**, who won it for his collection of poems titled **Odakkuzhal** (The Bamboo Flute) in the **Malayalam** language.

• The prize includes a cash award of **Rs. 11 lakh**, a citation plaque, and a bronze replica of **Vagdevi** (Saraswati), the goddess of learning.

• The **57th Jnanpith Award** was presented to **Damodar Mauzo**, a **Konkani** novelist and short story writer, in **2022**.

**Important Points__**

• **Ashapoorna Devi** was the **first woman** to receive the **Jnanpith Award** in **1976** for her **Bengali** novel **Pratham Pratishruti**.

• **Amitav Ghosh** became the **first author** to be honored with the **Jnanpith Award** for literature in the **English** language in **2018**.

• The **58th Jnanpith Award** (announced in **2024** for the year **2023**) marked only the **second time** the award was given for the **Sanskrit** language and the **fifth time** for the **Urdu** language.

• **R.K. Narayan** is often grouped with **Mulk Raj Anand** and **Raja Rao** as the **trinity of Indian English literature**, yet none of these three pioneers received the **Jnanpith Award**, as it was not open to **English** writers during their primary active years.
